title: 〜いかんによらず / いかんにかかわらず
content:
Romaji: ~ikan ni yorazu / ikan ni kakawarazu
Meaning: Regardless of ~ / irrespective of ~
Formation: Noun + のいかんによらず / のいかんにかかわらず
Explanation: Very formal expression meaning regardless of the nature or content of something.
Examples: 結果のいかんによらず、全力を尽くす。 - Regardless of the result, I will do my best. | 理由のいかんにかかわらず、遅刻は認めない。 - Regardless of the reason, lateness will not be tolerated.

title: 〜をもって
content:
Romaji: ~o motte
Meaning: With / by means of / as of (a time)
Formation: Noun + をもって
Explanation: Has two meanings: (1) by means of something, (2) as of a certain point in time (formal announcement).
Examples: 本日をもって、この店は閉店いたします。 - As of today, this store will close. | 実力をもって問題を解決した。 - Resolved the problem by means of ability.

title: 〜ならでは
content:
Romaji: ~naradewa
Meaning: Unique to / only possible with / characteristic of
Formation: Noun + ならでは（の）
Explanation: Expresses that something is exclusively characteristic of or only possible because of a particular subject.
Examples: 日本ならではの文化がある。 - There is a culture unique to Japan. | プロならではの技術だ。 - That is a technique only a professional could have.

title: 〜に足る
content:
Romaji: ~ni taru
Meaning: Worthy of / sufficient for / deserving
Formation: Verb dictionary form + に足る / に足りる
Explanation: Expresses that something meets the required standard or is worthy of a certain treatment.
Examples: 信頼するに足る人物だ。 - He is a person worthy of trust. | 評価するに足る作品だと思う。 - I think it is a work worthy of evaluation.

title: 〜とあって
content:
Romaji: ~to atte
Meaning: Because of the special circumstance that ~ / given that ~
Formation: Plain form + とあって
Explanation: Used when a special or unusual circumstance causes a particular result. The situation is noteworthy.
Examples: 三連休とあって、観光地は大混雑だった。 - Given that it was a three-day weekend, tourist spots were very crowded. | 人気アイドルの来日とあって、ファンが殺到した。 - Because of the popular idol's visit to Japan, fans flocked.

title: 〜を皮切りに（して）
content:
Romaji: ~o kawakiri ni (shite)
Meaning: Starting with ~ / beginning with ~ (as the first of many)
Formation: Noun + を皮切りに(して)
Explanation: Describes the first event in a series that triggers subsequent similar events.
Examples: 東京公演を皮切りに、全国ツアーが始まった。 - Starting with the Tokyo performance, the nationwide tour began. | A社を皮切りに、多くの企業が参入した。 - Starting with Company A, many companies entered the market.

title: 〜ともなると / ともなれば
content:
Romaji: ~to mo naru to / to mo nareba
Meaning: When it comes to ~ / once you become ~ (implying high expectations)
Formation: Noun + ともなると / ともなれば
Explanation: Expresses that at a certain high level or in a certain special position, certain things naturally follow.
Examples: 社長ともなると、責任も大きい。 - When you become a company president, responsibility also becomes great. | 有名人ともなれば、プライバシーがない。 - Once you become a celebrity, there is no privacy.

title: 〜といえども
content:
Romaji: ~to ie domo
Meaning: Even though / even if ~ (concessive, formal)
Formation: Plain form / Noun + といえども
Explanation: Even though a certain condition exists, the result is contrary to expectation. Very formal.
Examples: プロといえども、失敗することはある。 - Even a professional can fail sometimes. | 法律といえども、完璧ではない。 - Even the law is not perfect.

title: 〜ずにはおかない
content:
Romaji: ~zu ni wa okanai
Meaning: Cannot help but / will definitely cause / will inevitably do
Formation: Verb nai-stem + ずにはおかない
Explanation: Has two meanings: (1) something inevitably causes a reaction, (2) the speaker will definitely do something.
Examples: この映画は見る人を感動させずにはおかない。 - This movie cannot help but move its viewers. | 犯人を逮捕せずにはおかない。 - I will definitely arrest the criminal.

title: 〜にほかならない
content:
Romaji: ~ni hoka naranai
Meaning: Is nothing but / is precisely / is exactly
Formation: Noun / Plain form + にほかならない
Explanation: Asserts that something is precisely and nothing other than what is stated. Strong affirmation.
Examples: この成功は、チームの努力にほかならない。 - This success is nothing other than the team's effort. | 彼が来なかったのは、怠慢にほかならない。 - The reason he did not come is nothing but laziness.

title: 〜が最後
content:
Romaji: ~ga saigo
Meaning: Once ~ happens (there's no going back) / if ~ then it's all over
Formation: Verb た form + が最後
Explanation: Once a certain action takes place, an irreversible or extreme consequence follows.
Examples: 彼女に話しかけたが最後、一時間は止まらない。 - Once you start talking to her, she won't stop for an hour. | 借金をしたが最後、返済に苦しむことになる。 - Once you take on debt, you will suffer repaying it.

title: 〜べからず
content:
Romaji: ~bekarazu
Meaning: Must not / should not (prohibition, classical)
Formation: Verb dictionary form + べからず
Explanation: Classical prohibition form. Seen on signs and formal written rules.
Examples: 芝生に入るべからず。 - Do not enter the lawn. | 規則を破るべからず。 - One must not break the rules.

title: 〜てやまない
content:
Romaji: ~te yamanai
Meaning: Cannot stop ~ing / sincerely / from the bottom of one's heart
Formation: Verb て form + やまない
Explanation: Expresses a deep, unceasing feeling such as hope, love, or admiration.
Examples: 皆様のご活躍を願ってやみません。 - I sincerely hope for your continued success. | 彼の才能を愛してやまない。 - I cannot stop admiring his talent.

title: 〜ないまでも
content:
Romaji: ~nai made mo
Meaning: Even if not ~ at least / if not fully then at least partially
Formation: Verb nai form + までも
Explanation: Suggests settling for a lesser alternative when the ideal is not possible.
Examples: 毎日とは言わないまでも、週に一度は運動すべきだ。 - If not every day, at least you should exercise once a week. | 完璧でないまでも、最善を尽くした。 - If not perfect, at least I did my best.

title: 〜をものともせず
content:
Romaji: ~o mono to mo sezu
Meaning: Undaunted by / in spite of (adversity) / without being deterred by
Formation: Noun + をものともせず（に）
Explanation: Expresses that someone faced difficulties without being deterred — showing bravery or resilience.
Examples: 嵐をものともせず、船は前進した。 - Undaunted by the storm, the ship moved forward. | 批判をものともせず、改革を続けた。 - Undeterred by criticism, he continued the reforms.

title: 〜のみならず
content:
Romaji: ~nomi narazu
Meaning: Not only ~ but also (formal)
Formation: Noun / Plain form + のみならず
Explanation: Formal equivalent of〜だけでなく. Used in written Japanese and formal speech.
Examples: 国内のみならず、海外でも活躍している。 - They are active not only domestically but also abroad. | 経済のみならず、文化面でも発展した。 - Not only economically but also culturally, it developed.

title: 〜に即して
content:
Romaji: ~ni sokushite
Meaning: In accordance with / based on / in line with
Formation: Noun + に即して / に即した + Noun
Explanation: Indicates acting or thinking in direct accordance with rules, facts, or reality.
Examples: 法律に即して対処する。 - Deal with it in accordance with the law. | 現実に即した計画を立てる。 - Create a plan based on reality.

title: 〜そばから
content:
Romaji: ~soba kara
Meaning: As soon as / no sooner than (frustrating repetition)
Formation: Verb dictionary / た form + そばから
Explanation: Expresses frustration that as soon as one thing is done, the opposite immediately happens again.
Examples: 片付けるそばから、子供が散らかす。 - No sooner do I tidy up than the children make a mess again. | 覚えるそばから忘れてしまう。 - As soon as I memorize it, I forget it.

title: 〜ときたら
content:
Romaji: ~to kitara
Meaning: When it comes to ~ (expressing exasperation/complaint)
Formation: Noun + ときたら
Explanation: Used to introduce a topic about someone or something that the speaker is exasperated or dissatisfied with.
Examples: うちの息子ときたら、まったく勉強しない。 - When it comes to my son, he doesn't study at all. | 最近の若者ときたら、礼儀を知らない。 - When it comes to young people these days, they have no manners.

title: 〜ゆえに
content:
Romaji: ~yue ni
Meaning: Because of / therefore / due to (formal/literary)
Formation: Noun + の + ゆえに / Plain form + ゆえに
Explanation: Classical and formal expression of cause and reason. Literary equivalent of から or ので.
Examples: 若さゆえに、過ちを犯した。 - Due to youth, mistakes were made. | 無知ゆえに、傷つけてしまった。 - Because of ignorance, I ended up hurting someone.

title: 〜にもかかわらず
content:
Romaji: ~ni mo kakawarazu
Meaning: Despite / in spite of / regardless of
Formation: Noun / Verb (plain) / Adjective + にもかかわらず
Explanation: Used to express that something happened contrary to what was expected. Similar to のに but more formal.
Examples: 雨にもかかわらず、試合は行われた。 - Despite the rain, the game was held. | 努力したにもかかわらず、試験に落ちた。 - Despite making efforts, I failed the exam. | 忙しいにもかかわらず、来てくれた。 - Despite being busy, they came.

title: 〜をはじめ（として）
content:
Romaji: ~o hajime (toshite)
Meaning: Starting with / beginning with / including
Formation: Noun + をはじめ(として) + other nouns
Explanation: Used to give an example as a representative of a larger group.
Examples: 東京をはじめ、大阪や名古屋など多くの都市で販売される。 - It will be sold in many cities including Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya. | 社長をはじめ、社員全員が参加した。 - Starting with the president, all employees participated.

title: 〜に加えて
content:
Romaji: ~ni kuwaete
Meaning: In addition to / besides
Formation: Noun + に加えて
Explanation: Adds something extra on top of what was already mentioned.
Examples: 英語に加えて、日本語も話せます。 - In addition to English, I can also speak Japanese. | 寒さに加えて、風も強かった。 - In addition to the cold, the wind was also strong.

title: 〜かねない
content:
Romaji: ~kanenai
Meaning: Might possibly (undesirable result); cannot be ruled out
Formation: Verb stem + かねない
Explanation: Expresses concern that something undesirable might happen.
Examples: このまま放置すると、大事故になりかねない。 - If left like this, it could possibly lead to a serious accident. | 彼は嘘をつきかねない人だ。 - He is the kind of person who might lie.

title: 〜をめぐって
content:
Romaji: ~o megutte
Meaning: Surrounding / concerning / over (a controversial topic)
Formation: Noun + をめぐって / をめぐる + Noun
Explanation: Used when multiple parties have differing views or conflicts about a topic.
Examples: 予算をめぐって激しい議論が行われた。 - A heated debate took place over the budget. | 領土をめぐる問題は複雑だ。 - The issue surrounding the territory is complex.

title: 〜に際して
content:
Romaji: ~ni saishite
Meaning: At the time of / on the occasion of / when doing
Formation: Noun / Verb dictionary form + に際して
Explanation: Used for important, formal, or special occasions. More formal than〜とき.
Examples: 入学に際して、保護者の同意が必要です。 - At the time of enrollment, parental consent is required. | 契約を結ぶに際して、内容をよく確認してください。 - When signing a contract, please confirm the contents carefully.

title: 〜に反して
content:
Romaji: ~ni hanshite
Meaning: Contrary to / against / in opposition to
Formation: Noun + に反して / に反する + Noun
Explanation: Indicates that something goes against an expectation, rule, or wish.
Examples: 予想に反して、試験は簡単だった。 - Contrary to expectations, the exam was easy. | 親の意志に反して、芸術家になった。 - Going against his parents' wishes, he became an artist.

title: 〜を通じて / を通して
content:
Romaji: ~o tsujite / o tooshite
Meaning: Through / throughout / by means of
Formation: Noun + を通じて / を通して
Explanation: Expresses a medium or method by which something is done, or indicates throughout a period.
Examples: インターネットを通じて情報を集める。 - Gather information through the internet. | 一年を通じて温暖な気候だ。 - It has a warm climate throughout the year.

title: 〜末に
content:
Romaji: ~sue ni
Meaning: After (a long process) / at the end of
Formation: Verb た form / Noun + の + 末に
Explanation: Used to express something that occurred after a long period of effort or deliberation.
Examples: 長い議論の末に、結論が出た。 - After a long discussion, a conclusion was reached. | 悩んだ末に、会社を辞めることにした。 - After much deliberation, I decided to quit the company.

title: 〜にわたって
content:
Romaji: ~ni watatte
Meaning: Spanning / covering / throughout (range or period)
Formation: Noun (time/range) + にわたって / にわたる + Noun
Explanation: Describes something that extends across a range of time, distance, or area.
Examples: 三日間にわたって会議が続いた。 - The conference continued for three days. | 広い範囲にわたる調査が行われた。 - An investigation spanning a wide area was conducted.

title: 〜に対して
content:
Romaji: ~ni taishite
Meaning: Toward / against / in contrast to / regarding
Formation: Noun + に対して / に対する + Noun
Explanation: Can express direction of action/feeling, contrast, or response toward something.
Examples: 先生に対して失礼な態度をとった。 - He took a rude attitude toward the teacher. | 兄が背が高いのに対して、弟は低い。 - In contrast to his tall older brother, the younger one is short.

title: 〜というより
content:
Romaji: ~to iu yori
Meaning: Rather than saying ~ / more ~ than ~
Formation: Phrase A + というより + Phrase B
Explanation: Used to correct or refine a description, suggesting B is more accurate than A.
Examples: 彼は怒っているというより、悲しんでいる。 - Rather than angry, he is sad. | これは趣味というより、仕事だ。 - This is more of a job than a hobby.

title: 〜上で
content:
Romaji: ~ue de
Meaning: In order to / after doing / in terms of / when it comes to
Formation: Verb dictionary/た form + 上で / Noun + の + 上で
Explanation: Used to express a prerequisite action or a consideration in a certain context.
Examples: 契約する上で、注意すべき点がある。 - There are points to be careful of when signing a contract. | 話し合った上で、決定します。 - We will decide after discussing.

title: 〜をきっかけに
content:
Romaji: ~o kikkake ni
Meaning: Taking ~ as a trigger / using ~ as a chance
Formation: Noun + をきっかけに(して)
Explanation: Describes an event that became the trigger or turning point for a change.
Examples: この事故をきっかけに、安全対策が強化された。 - Using this accident as a trigger, safety measures were strengthened. | 留学をきっかけに、英語が好きになった。 - Studying abroad triggered my love for English.

title: 〜からといって
content:
Romaji: ~kara to itte
Meaning: Just because ~ (doesn't mean)
Formation: Verb / Adjective / Noun plain form + からといって
Explanation: Used to say that even though reason A exists, conclusion B doesn't necessarily follow.
Examples: お金があるからといって、幸せとは限らない。 - Just because you have money doesn't mean you're happy. | 忙しいからといって、食事を抜いてはいけない。 - Just because you're busy, you shouldn't skip meals.

title: 〜次第
content:
Romaji: ~shidai
Meaning: As soon as / depending on / up to
Formation: Verb stem + 次第 / Noun + 次第
Explanation: Verb stem + 次第 means "as soon as done." Noun + 次第 means "depending on."
Examples: 準備ができ次第、出発します。 - We will depart as soon as preparations are complete. | 結果は努力次第だ。 - The result depends on your effort.

title: 〜ものの
content:
Romaji: ~mono no
Meaning: Although / even though (but the result is contrary)
Formation: Verb / Adjective plain form + ものの
Explanation: Concedes a fact in the first clause but introduces a contrasting or disappointing reality.
Examples: 勉強したものの、試験に落ちた。 - Although I studied, I failed the exam. | 申し込んだものの、まだ返事がない。 - Although I applied, I have not received a reply yet.

title: 〜に伴って
content:
Romaji: ~ni tomonatte
Meaning: Along with / as ~ increases / accompanying
Formation: Noun / Verb dictionary form + に伴って / に伴い
Explanation: Expresses that as one thing changes, another thing changes proportionally alongside it.
Examples: 経済成長に伴って、生活水準が上がった。 - Along with economic growth, the standard of living rose. | 人口増加に伴い、住宅不足が深刻化している。 - Accompanying the population increase, housing shortages are becoming serious.

title: 〜において / における
content:
Romaji: ~ni oite / ni okeru
Meaning: In / at / regarding (formal location/context)
Formation: Noun + において / における + Noun
Explanation: Formal equivalent of で when indicating a place, situation, or field of activity.
Examples: 現代社会において、情報は非常に重要だ。 - In modern society, information is extremely important. | 教育における問題を議論する。 - Discuss problems in education.

title: 〜にとって
content:
Romaji: ~ni totte
Meaning: For / from the perspective of
Formation: Noun + にとって
Explanation: Expresses a standpoint or perspective from which something is evaluated.
Examples: 子供にとって、遊びは大切な学びだ。 - For children, play is important learning. | 私にとって、家族が一番大切です。 - For me, family is the most important.

title: 〜わけではない
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: It doesn't mean that ~ / It's not that ~
Formation: Plain form + わけではない／わけじゃない
Explanation: Used to deny or partially deny an implication. Clarifies a misunderstanding or nuances a statement.
Examples: 嫌いなわけではないが、あまり食べない。 - It's not that I dislike it, I just don't eat much of it. | 難しいわけじゃないけど、時間がかかる。 - It's not that it's difficult, it just takes time.

title: 〜にもかかわらず
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Despite ~ / In spite of ~ / Nevertheless
Formation: Noun / Verb plain form + にもかかわらず
Explanation: 
Examples: 雨にもかかわらず、試合は続けられた。 - Despite the rain, the match continued.

title: 〜に対して
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Towards ~ / Against ~ / In contrast to ~
Formation: Noun + に対して
Explanation: 
Examples: 先生の質問に対して答えました。 - I answered the teacher's question. | 彼が賛成なのに対して、私は反対だ。 - In contrast to him being in favor, I am opposed.

title: 〜によって
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: By means of ~ / Depending on ~ / Due to ~
Formation: Noun + によって
Explanation: 
Examples: この絵はピカソによって描かれました。 - This painting was drawn by Picasso. | 結果は努力によって変わる。 - Results change depending on effort.

title: 〜として
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: As ~ / In the role/capacity of ~
Formation: Noun + として
Explanation: 
Examples: 医者として働いています。 - I work as a doctor. | 友達として彼女を助けたい。 - I want to help her as a friend.

title: 〜ばかり
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Just did ~ (recently) / Only ~ / Nothing but ~
Formation: Verb た-form / Noun + ばかり
Explanation: 
Examples: 今来たばかりです。 - I just arrived. | 彼はゲームばかりしている。 - He does nothing but play games.

title: 〜さえ〜ば
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: If only ~ / As long as ~ (minimum condition)
Formation: Noun + さえ / Verb stem + さえすれば
Explanation: 
Examples: お金さえあれば何でも買える。 - If only I had money, I could buy anything. | 健康でさえあれば幸せだ。 - As long as I'm healthy, I'm happy.

title: 〜ものの
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Although ~ / Even though ~ (but the result is unexpected)
Formation: Plain form + ものの
Explanation: 
Examples: 日本語を勉強したものの、まだ話せない。 - Although I studied Japanese, I still can't speak it.

title: 〜だけでなく〜も
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Not only ~ but also ~
Formation: Noun / Plain form + だけでなく ~ も
Explanation: 
Examples: 彼女は英語だけでなく、日本語も話せます。 - She can speak not only English but also Japanese.

title: 〜てしまう
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Completely finish / Accidentally do / Regrettably do
Formation: Verb て-form + しまう／ちゃう (casual)
Explanation: 
Examples: 宿題をやってしまいました。 - I finished my homework (completely). | 財布を忘れちゃった。 - I accidentally forgot my wallet!

title: 〜ことになっている
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: It has been decided that ~ / It is expected that ~ (rule/schedule)
Formation: Verb plain form + ことになっている
Explanation: 
Examples: 明日会議があることになっています。 - There is supposed to be a meeting tomorrow. | ここでは靴を脱ぐことになっている。 - The rule here is that you take off your shoes.

title: 〜わけがない
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: There is no way that ~ / Cannot possibly ~
Formation: Plain form + わけがない／わけはない
Explanation: 
Examples: 彼がそんなことを言うわけがない。 - There is no way he would say such a thing.

title: 〜ところ
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Just about to ~ / In the middle of ~ / Just finished ~
Formation: Verb various forms + ところ
Explanation: Dictionary form + ところ = about to do. ている + ところ = in the middle of doing. た + ところ = just finished doing.
Examples: 今から出かけるところです。 - I am about to go out now. | ご飯を食べているところです。 - I am in the middle of eating. | 今来たところです。 - I just arrived.

title: 〜とともに
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Together with ~ / As ~ / Along with ~
Formation: Noun / Verb dictionary form + とともに
Explanation: 
Examples: 時代の変化とともに、技術も進歩した。 - Along with the changes of the era, technology also advanced.

title: 〜に加えて
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: In addition to ~ / On top of ~
Formation: Noun + に加えて
Explanation: 
Examples: 雨に加えて、風も強かった。 - In addition to rain, the wind was also strong.

title: 〜てあげる／てくれる／てもらう
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Giving/receiving actions (I do for you / you do for me / I receive the favor of)
Formation: Verb て-form + あげる／くれる／もらう
Explanation: あげる: I/someone gives action TO another. くれる: someone gives action TO me. もらう: I receive the action FROM someone.
Examples: 荷物を持ってあげました。 - I carried the luggage (for them). | 先生が教えてくれました。 - The teacher taught me. | 友達に手伝ってもらいました。 - I had my friend help me.

title: 〜ば〜のに
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: If only ~ / I wish ~ (expressing regret)
Formation: Verb conditional ば + のに
Explanation: 
Examples: もっと勉強すればよかったのに。 - I wish I had studied more.

title: 〜そうです（様態）
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Looks like ~ / seems ~ (appearance-based conjecture)
Formation: Verb/Adj stem + そうです
Explanation: Used when you can visually observe that something seems a certain way. Different from the hearsay そうです.
Examples: このケーキは美味しそうです。 - This cake looks delicious. | 雨が降りそうです。 - It looks like it will rain.

title: 〜らしい
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Apparently ~ / It seems ~ (hearsay/inference from evidence)
Formation: Verb/Noun/Adj plain form + らしい
Explanation: 
Examples: 田中さんは来ないらしいです。 - It seems Tanaka is not coming.

title: 〜ようだ
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: It appears that ~ (inference based on observation)
Formation: Verb/Adj plain form + ようだ
Explanation: 
Examples: 彼は疲れているようです。 - He appears to be tired.

title: 〜でしょう／だろう
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Probably ~ / I wonder if ~ (conjecture/uncertainty)
Formation: Sentence + でしょう (polite) / だろう (plain)
Explanation: 
Examples: 明日は雨でしょう。 - It will probably rain tomorrow. | 彼は来るだろう。 - He will probably come.

title: 〜かもしれない
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Maybe ~ / might ~ (possibility, less certain than でしょう)
Formation: Plain form + かもしれない／かもしれません
Explanation: 
Examples: 明日は雪かもしれません。 - It might snow tomorrow. | 彼女は知らないかもしれない。 - She might not know.

title: 〜なければならない
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Must do ~ / have to do ~
Formation: Verb negative stem + なければならない
Explanation: Expresses obligation or necessity. Casual forms: なきゃ、なくちゃ. Negative: なくてもいい (don't have to).
Examples: 毎日薬を飲まなければなりません。 - I must take medicine every day. | 早く起きなきゃ。 - I have to wake up early. (casual)

title: 〜てもいい
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: It's okay to ~ / May I ~ (permission)
Formation: Verb て-form + もいい／もいいです
Explanation: 
Examples: ここに座ってもいいですか。 - May I sit here? | 写真を撮ってもいいです。 - You may take photos.

title: 〜てはいけない
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Must not ~ / Not allowed to ~
Formation: Verb て-form + はいけない／はいけません
Explanation: 
Examples: ここでタバコを吸ってはいけません。 - You must not smoke here. | 試験中に話してはいけない。 - Don't talk during the exam.

title: 〜たことがある
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Have done ~ before (past experience)
Formation: Verb た-form + ことがある
Explanation: 
Examples: 富士山に登ったことがあります。 - I have climbed Mt. Fuji before. | 寿司を食べたことがありますか。 - Have you ever eaten sushi?

title: 〜ながら
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: While doing ~ (two simultaneous actions by same person)
Formation: Verb stem + ながら
Explanation: 
Examples: 音楽を聞きながら勉強します。 - I study while listening to music. | 歩きながらスマホを見るのは危ない。 - Looking at your phone while walking is dangerous.

title: 〜と思う
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: I think that ~ (expressing opinion)
Formation: Plain form + と思う／と思います
Explanation: 
Examples: 彼は正しいと思います。 - I think he is right. | 明日は晴れると思う。 - I think it will be sunny tomorrow.

title: 〜ために
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: In order to ~ / for the purpose of ~
Formation: Verb dictionary form / Noun の + ために
Explanation: 
Examples: 日本語を学ぶために日本に来ました。 - I came to Japan in order to learn Japanese. | 健康のために運動します。 - I exercise for my health.

title: 〜ように
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: So that ~ / in order to ~ (goal/purpose for intransitive verbs)
Formation: Verb dictionary/negative + ように
Explanation: 
Examples: 日本語が上手になるように毎日練習します。 - I practice every day so that my Japanese improves. | 遅刻しないように早く出ました。 - I left early so as not to be late.

title: 〜は〜です
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Topic marker + copula (is/am/are)
Formation: Noun は Noun/Adjective です
Explanation: Used to state facts about the topic. は (wa) marks the topic of the sentence. です (desu) is a polite sentence-ending that means 'is/am/are'.
Examples: 私は学生です。 - I am a student. | これは本です。 - This is a book. | 田中さんは先生です。 - Mr. Tanaka is a teacher.

title: 〜は〜ではありません
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Negative form of です (is not)
Formation: Noun は Noun ではありません
Explanation: The negative of 〜です. In casual speech, じゃないです or じゃありません can also be used.
Examples: 私は先生ではありません。 - I am not a teacher. | これはペンじゃないです。 - This is not a pen. | 田中さんは学生ではありません。 - Mr. Tanaka is not a student.

title: 〜が〜です
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Subject marker が — marks the subject performing the action
Formation: Noun が Adjective/Verb
Explanation: が marks the grammatical subject. Unlike は which marks the topic, が focuses on who/what performs the action or has the quality.
Examples: 猫が好きです。 - I like cats. (Cats are what I like.) | 雨が降っています。 - It is raining. | 山田さんが来ました。 - Mr. Yamada came.

title: 〜を〜します
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Object marker を — marks the direct object of a transitive verb
Formation: Noun を Verb
Explanation: を (pronounced 'o') marks the direct object — the thing that receives the action of a transitive verb.
Examples: ご飯を食べます。 - I eat rice/a meal. | 本を読みます。 - I read a book. | 日本語を勉強します。 - I study Japanese.

title: 〜に〜があります／います
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Existence: there is/are (あります for inanimate, います for animate)
Formation: Place に Thing/Person が あります／います
Explanation: Use あります for non-living things and います for living things (people, animals). The location is marked with に.
Examples: 机の上に本があります。 - There is a book on the desk. | 公園に子供がいます。 - There are children in the park. | 冷蔵庫にジュースがあります。 - There is juice in the refrigerator.

title: 〜で〜します
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: で marks location of action OR means/method
Formation: Place で Verb / Means で Verb
Explanation: で has two key uses: (1) marks where an action takes place, (2) marks the means or tool used to do something.
Examples: 図書館で勉強します。 - I study at the library. | バスで来ました。 - I came by bus. | 日本語で話してください。 - Please speak in Japanese.

title: 〜に行きます／来ます／帰ります
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Direction marker に with movement verbs (go/come/return to)
Formation: Place に Verb of movement
Explanation: に marks the destination with verbs of movement like 行く (go), 来る (come), 帰る (return). The particle へ can also be used interchangeably in most cases.
Examples: 学校に行きます。 - I go to school. | 家に帰ります。 - I return home. | 日本に来ました。 - I came to Japan.

title: 〜たいです
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Want to do ~ (expressing desire)
Formation: Verb stem + たいです
Explanation: Attach たい to the verb stem (remove ます from masu-form). The result is treated like an い-adjective. Negative: たくないです. Past: たかったです.
Examples: 日本に行きたいです。 - I want to go to Japan. | 寿司を食べたいです。 - I want to eat sushi. | 日本語を話したいです。 - I want to speak Japanese.

title: 〜ましょう
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Let's do ~ (making a suggestion or invitation)
Formation: Verb stem + ましょう
Explanation: ましょう is the volitional/hortative form. It suggests doing something together. ましょうか is softer: 'Shall we?'
Examples: 一緒に食べましょう。 - Let's eat together. | 映画を見ましょう。 - Let's watch a movie. | 休みましょうか。 - Shall we rest?

title: 〜てください
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Please do ~ (polite request)
Formation: Verb て-form + ください
Explanation: Form the て-form of the verb and add ください. This is a standard polite way to make requests.
Examples: ここに座ってください。 - Please sit here. | ゆっくり話してください。 - Please speak slowly. | 名前を書いてください。 - Please write your name.

title: 〜ている
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Currently doing ~ OR state resulting from action
Formation: Verb て-form + いる／います
Explanation: Two main uses: (1) ongoing action — I am doing something right now; (2) resultant state — a state that results from a completed action (married, know, wearing).
Examples: 今、本を読んでいます。 - I am reading a book now. | 田中さんは結婚しています。 - Mr. Tanaka is married. | 赤いシャツを着ています。 - He/She is wearing a red shirt.

title: 〜た形 (Past tense)
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Past tense of verbs
Formation: Verb た-form
Explanation: The た-form indicates completed actions. For polite speech, use ました. For plain/casual speech, use た directly.
Examples: 昨日、映画を見ました。 - Yesterday, I watched a movie. | ご飯を食べた。 - I ate a meal. (casual) | 昨日は雨が降りました。 - It rained yesterday.

title: 〜ないでください
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Please don't do ~
Formation: Verb negative stem + ないでください
Explanation: Attach ないで to the nai-form (negative plain form) of a verb, then add ください. Used to politely ask someone not to do something.
Examples: ここで写真を撮らないでください。 - Please don't take photos here. | 遅刻しないでください。 - Please don't be late. | 心配しないでください。 - Please don't worry.

title: 〜から〜まで
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: From ~ to ~ (time or place range)
Formation: Start から End まで
Explanation: から marks the starting point and まで marks the end point. Can be used with time (9 o'clock to 5) or place (Tokyo to Osaka).
Examples: 9時から5時まで働きます。 - I work from 9 to 5. | 東京から大阪まで新幹線で行きます。 - I go from Tokyo to Osaka by Shinkansen. | 月曜日から金曜日まで学校があります。 - School is from Monday to Friday.

title: 〜も
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Also/too ~ (inclusive particle)
Formation: Noun も
Explanation: も replaces は, が, or を to mean 'also' or 'too'. When used with negatives it means 'neither/either': 〜もありません.
Examples: 私も学生です。 - I am also a student. | コーヒーも飲みます。 - I also drink coffee. | 猫も犬も好きです。 - I like both cats and dogs.

title: 〜の
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Possessive/descriptive connector
Formation: Noun の Noun
Explanation: の connects two nouns, showing possession (my book), origin (Japanese music), or description (coffee shop). The modifier always comes before の.
Examples: 私の本です。 - It is my book. | 日本の音楽が好きです。 - I like Japanese music. | これは田中さんの傘です。 - This is Mr. Tanaka's umbrella.

title: 〜や〜など
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: And ~ and ~ etc. (non-exhaustive list)
Formation: Noun や Noun など
Explanation: や lists examples from a larger group (implying 'and things like these'). など adds 'etc.' or 'and so on'. Contrast with と which lists everything exhaustively.
Examples: 果物や野菜などを買いました。 - I bought fruits, vegetables, and so on. | 日本語や英語などを勉強しています。 - I am studying Japanese, English, and so on. | 東京や大阪などに行きたいです。 - I want to go to Tokyo, Osaka, and places like that.

title: 〜と〜
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: And ~ (exhaustive listing) / With ~ / Quotation と
Formation: Noun と Noun / Verb plain form + と
Explanation: と has three uses: (1) lists nouns exhaustively (A and B, nothing else), (2) marks a companion (with someone), (3) marks a quotation or thought before 言う/思う.
Examples: りんごとみかんを食べました。 - I ate an apple and a mandarin orange. | 友達と映画を見ました。 - I watched a movie with my friend. | 彼は「おはよう」と言いました。 - He said 'Good morning'.

title: 〜ね／〜よ
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: ね = seeking agreement / よ = asserting information
Formation: Sentence + ね / よ
Explanation: ね is used when you expect the listener to agree or share the same feeling. よ asserts information the listener may not know. よね combines both.
Examples: 今日は暑いですね。 - It's hot today, isn't it? | これは美味しいですよ。 - This is delicious, I tell you! | 明日、テストがありますよね。 - There's a test tomorrow, right?

title: 〜か
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Question marker (turns statement into question)
Formation: Sentence + か
Explanation: か at the end of a sentence makes it a question. In polite speech (〜ますか、〜ですか) the intonation stays flat. In casual speech, just raise the intonation.
Examples: これは何ですか。 - What is this? | 日本人ですか。 - Are you Japanese? | 明日、学校に来ますか。 - Will you come to school tomorrow?

title: 〜てから
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: After doing ~ (sequential actions)
Formation: Verb て-form + から
Explanation: Indicates that one action is completed before the next begins. The て-form + から emphasises that the first action is fully done before the second starts.
Examples: 手を洗ってから、ご飯を食べます。 - After washing my hands, I eat. | 宿題をしてから、遊びます。 - After doing homework, I play. | シャワーを浴びてから、寝ます。 - After taking a shower, I sleep.

title: 〜たり〜たりします
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Do things like ~ and ~ (non-exhaustive list of actions)
Formation: Verb た-form + り … Verb た-form + りします
Explanation: Lists representative activities without implying it's a complete list. Form: change verb to た-form, add り, repeat for other verbs, end with します.
Examples: 週末は映画を見たり、音楽を聴いたりします。 - On weekends I do things like watch movies and listen to music. | 日本語を読んだり、書いたりします。 - I do things like read and write Japanese. | 旅行では写真を撮ったり、食べ物を食べたりしました。 - On the trip I did things like take photos and eat food.

title: 〜ことができる
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Can do ~ / be able to do ~ (ability or possibility)
Formation: Verb dictionary form + ことができる
Explanation: Expresses ability or possibility. The simpler alternative is the potential verb form (食べられる). ことができる is slightly more formal.
Examples: 日本語を話すことができます。 - I can speak Japanese. | ここで泳ぐことができますか。 - Can we swim here? | 漢字を読むことができません。 - I cannot read kanji.

title: 〜前に
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Before doing ~ (prior action)
Formation: Verb dictionary form / Noun + の + 前に
Explanation: 前に with a verb (dictionary form) means 'before doing'. With a noun, use の前に. The action in 前に clause is not yet completed.
Examples: 寝る前に歯を磨きます。 - I brush my teeth before sleeping. | 食事の前に手を洗います。 - I wash my hands before meals. | 日本に来る前に、日本語を勉強しました。 - Before coming to Japan, I studied Japanese.

title: 〜後で
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: After doing ~ (subsequent action)
Formation: Verb た-form / Noun + の + 後で
Explanation: 後で indicates an action happens after another. With verbs, use the た-form. With nouns, use の後で.
Examples: 授業が終わった後で、図書館に行きます。 - After class ends, I will go to the library. | 仕事の後で、飲みに行きましょう。 - After work, let's go for a drink. | 昼ご飯を食べた後で、散歩しました。 - After eating lunch, I took a walk.

title: い-adjective conjugation
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: い-adjective: negative, past, and negative past forms
Formation: い-adj (〜い) → 〜くない / 〜かった / 〜くなかった
Explanation: い-adjectives conjugate by changing the final い: drop い and add くない (neg), かった (past), くなかった (neg past). Exception: いい → よい → よくない / よかった.
Examples: この映画は面白くないです。 - This movie is not interesting. | 昨日は寒かったです。 - It was cold yesterday. | その料理は美味しくなかったです。 - That dish was not delicious.

title: な-adjective conjugation
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: な-adjective: negative, past, and negative past forms
Formation: な-adj + です → じゃない / でした / じゃなかった
Explanation: な-adjectives conjugate like nouns + です. Negative: じゃありません/ではありません. Past: でした. Neg past: じゃありませんでした.
Examples: この部屋は静かじゃないです。 - This room is not quiet. | 彼女はとても元気でした。 - She was very energetic. | その公園はあまり有名じゃなかったです。 - That park was not very famous.

title: 〜より〜のほうが
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: B is more ~ than A (comparison)
Formation: A より B のほうが Adjective
Explanation: より marks the standard of comparison (A). のほうが marks what is being compared favourably (B). The adjective follows.
Examples: 犬より猫のほうが好きです。 - I like cats more than dogs. | 電車よりバスのほうが安いです。 - The bus is cheaper than the train. | 夏より冬のほうが好きです。 - I like winter more than summer.

title: 〜が一番
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: ~ is the most / ~ is number one (superlative)
Formation: Noun が 一番 Adjective
Explanation: 一番 (いちばん) means 'number one' or 'most'. Place it before the adjective. To specify the group, use 〜の中で〜が一番.
Examples: 日本語が一番難しいです。 - Japanese is the most difficult. | クラスの中で山田さんが一番背が高いです。 - In the class, Mr. Yamada is the tallest. | 季節の中で、春が一番好きです。 - Among seasons, I like spring the most.

title: 〜から (reason)
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Because ~ / Since ~ (stating a reason)
Formation: Plain form / Polite form + から
Explanation: から after a clause gives the reason for what follows. In polite speech, both clauses use polite forms. In casual speech, plain forms are used.
Examples: 眠いから、早く寝ます。 - Because I am sleepy, I will sleep early. | 雨が降っているから、傘を持ってください。 - Because it is raining, please take an umbrella. | 日本語が好きだから、毎日勉強します。 - Because I like Japanese, I study every day.

title: 〜ので
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Because ~ / Since ~ (softer, objective reason)
Formation: Plain form (な-adj/Noun + な) + ので
Explanation: ので gives a reason like から but sounds more objective and polite. Better for formal situations. な-adjectives and nouns use なので before ので.
Examples: 疲れたので、休みます。 - Since I am tired, I will rest. | 病気なので、学校を休みました。 - Since I was sick, I was absent from school. | 明日試験があるので、今日は早く寝ます。 - Since there is an exam tomorrow, I will sleep early today.

title: 〜が、〜 (contrast)
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: ~ but ~ (contrast between two clauses)
Formation: Clause 1 + が、Clause 2
Explanation: が as a conjunction connects two contrasting clauses like 'but' or 'however'. It can also soften a statement without strong contrast.
Examples: 日本語は面白いですが、難しいです。 - Japanese is interesting but difficult. | 高いですが、美味しいです。 - It's expensive but delicious. | 行きたいですが、時間がありません。 - I want to go but I don't have time.

title: どんな〜
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: What kind of ~ (asking about characteristics)
Formation: どんな + Noun
Explanation: どんな asks about the type or quality of something. Similar to 'what kind of' in English.
Examples: どんな音楽が好きですか。 - What kind of music do you like? | どんな人が好きですか。 - What kind of person do you like? | 日本はどんな国ですか。 - What kind of country is Japan?

title: 〜くなる / 〜になる
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: To become ~ (change of state)
Formation: い-adj stem + くなる / な-adj or Noun + になる
Explanation: なる means 'to become'. い-adjectives change い to くなる. な-adjectives and nouns use になる.
Examples: 春になると、暖かくなります。 - When spring comes, it becomes warm. | 日本語が上手になりたいです。 - I want to become good at Japanese. | 大人になったら、医者になりたい。 - When I grow up, I want to become a doctor.

title: 〜てもいいです
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: It is okay to ~ / You may ~ (giving or asking permission)
Formation: Verb て-form + もいいです
Explanation: 〜てもいいです gives permission. 〜てもいいですか asks for permission. To deny: 〜てはいけません or 〜てはだめです.
Examples: ここで食べてもいいですか。 - May I eat here? | 窓を開けてもいいです。 - You may open the window. | この本を借りてもいいですか。 - May I borrow this book?

title: 〜てはいけません
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Must not ~ / It is not allowed to ~ (prohibition)
Formation: Verb て-form + はいけません
Explanation: 〜てはいけません prohibits an action. More forceful than 〜ないでください. Common in rules and regulations.
Examples: ここでタバコを吸ってはいけません。 - You must not smoke here. | 授業中に携帯を使ってはいけません。 - You must not use your phone during class. | 嘘をついてはいけません。 - You must not lie.

title: 〜なければなりません
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Must ~ / Have to ~ (obligation)
Formation: Verb nai-stem + なければなりません
Explanation: Expresses obligation. Formed by changing ない to なければ and adding なりません. Casual: 〜なきゃ or 〜なければ.
Examples: 明日、早く起きなければなりません。 - I must wake up early tomorrow. | 宿題をしなければなりません。 - I have to do my homework. | 薬を飲まなければなりません。 - I must take the medicine.

title: 〜でしょう / 〜だろう
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Probably ~ / I think ~ (conjecture)
Formation: Plain form + でしょう / だろう
Explanation: Expresses probability or supposition. でしょう is polite; だろう is plain/casual. Often used with たぶん (probably).
Examples: 明日は雨が降るでしょう。 - It will probably rain tomorrow. | 彼は来ないだろう。 - He probably won't come. | たぶん大丈夫でしょう。 - It will probably be fine.

title: 〜と思います
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: I think that ~ (expressing opinion or belief)
Formation: Plain form + と思います
Explanation: Used to express the speaker's opinion or belief. The clause before と is always in plain form. と思っています implies ongoing thinking.
Examples: 日本語は面白いと思います。 - I think Japanese is interesting. | 明日は晴れると思います。 - I think it will be sunny tomorrow. | 彼女は来ないと思います。 - I think she will not come.

title: 〜そうです (hearsay)
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: I heard that ~ / They say that ~ (hearsay)
Formation: Plain form + そうです
Explanation: Reports information heard from others. Always in plain form before そうです. Different from そうです (appearance) which uses verb stem/adj stem.
Examples: 田中さんは来月結婚するそうです。 - I heard that Mr. Tanaka will get married next month. | 明日は休みだそうです。 - I heard that tomorrow is a holiday. | あのレストランは美味しいそうです。 - I heard that restaurant is delicious.

title: 〜時
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: When ~ / At the time of ~
Formation: Verb / Adjective plain form + 時 / Noun + の + 時
Explanation: 時 (とき) means 'time' or 'when'. Use verb dictionary form for future/habitual events, た-form for completed events.
Examples: 子供の時、よく公園で遊びました。 - When I was a child, I often played in the park. | 日本に来た時、富士山を見ました。 - When I came to Japan, I saw Mt. Fuji. | 暇な時、映画を見ます。 - When I have free time, I watch movies.

title: 毎〜 (frequency words)
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Every ~ (daily, weekly, monthly etc.)
Formation: 毎 + time noun
Explanation: 毎 (まい) means 'every'. Common forms: 毎日 (every day), 毎週 (every week), 毎月 (every month), 毎年 (every year), 毎朝 (every morning), 毎晩 (every evening).
Examples: 毎日日本語を勉強します。 - I study Japanese every day. | 毎週映画を見ます。 - I watch a movie every week. | 毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。 - I drink coffee every morning.

title: 〜ごろ / 〜ぐらい
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Around ~ / About ~ (approximate time or quantity)
Formation: Time/Number + ごろ / ぐらい (くらい)
Explanation: ごろ is used for approximate points in time. ぐらい/くらい is used for approximate amounts or durations.
Examples: 7時ごろ起きます。 - I wake up around 7 o'clock. | 一時間ぐらい勉強しました。 - I studied for about one hour. | 来週ごろ、返事をします。 - I will reply around next week.

title: 〜番目 (ordinal numbers)
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: ~th / ~st / ~nd / ~rd (ordinal numbers)
Formation: Number + 番目
Explanation: 番目 makes ordinal numbers. 一番目 (first), 二番目 (second). In some contexts, 番目 is dropped: 一番 (number one/most).
Examples: 私は三番目に到着しました。 - I arrived third. | 左から二番目の人が田中さんです。 - The second person from the left is Mr. Tanaka. | これが一番目の質問です。 - This is the first question.

title: 〜くらい / 〜ほど (degree)
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: About ~ / To the extent of ~ (degree or comparison)
Formation: Noun / Amount + くらい / ほど
Explanation: Both express degree or extent. ほど is more formal and also used in comparisons: 〜ほど〜ない (not as ~ as).
Examples: 死ぬほど疲れました。 - I was so tired I could die. | 彼女ほど優しい人はいません。 - There is no one as kind as her. | 一時間くらい待ちました。 - I waited for about an hour.

title: あげる / もらう / くれる
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Giving and receiving actions (directional verbs)
Formation: Verb て-form + あげる / もらう / くれる
Explanation: あげる = give (to others), もらう = receive (from others), くれる = give (to me/my group). These determine the direction of giving.
Examples: 友達にプレゼントをあげました。 - I gave a present to my friend. | 先生に本をもらいました。 - I received a book from my teacher. | 母が手紙を書いてくれました。 - My mother wrote a letter for me.

title: 〜と言います
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Say that ~ / be called ~ (quoting or naming)
Formation: Quoted speech + と言います / と言いました
Explanation: と言います quotes direct or indirect speech. Also used to say what something is called: 〜と言います means 'is called ~'.
Examples: 私の名前は田中と言います。 - My name is Tanaka (lit: I am called Tanaka). | 彼は「明日来ます」と言いました。 - He said 'I will come tomorrow'. | これは日本語で何と言いますか。 - How do you say this in Japanese?

title: 〜方 (〜かた)
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: The way of doing ~ / How to do ~
Formation: Verb stem + 方
Explanation: 方 (かた) attached to a verb stem means 'the way of doing' or 'how to do'. 食べ方 = the way of eating, 書き方 = how to write.
Examples: この漢字の書き方を教えてください。 - Please teach me how to write this kanji. | 納豆の食べ方が分かりません。 - I don't know how to eat natto. | この電話の使い方を教えてもらえますか。 - Could you tell me how to use this phone?

title: 〜すぎる
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Too ~ / Excessively ~ (excess)
Formation: い-adj stem / な-adj stem / Verb stem + すぎる
Explanation: すぎる means 'too much' or 'excessively'. Attach to い-adj stem (remove い), な-adj stem, or verb stem (remove ます).
Examples: この料理は辛すぎます。 - This dish is too spicy. | 昨日、食べすぎました。 - I ate too much yesterday. | この服は私には大きすぎます。 - These clothes are too big for me.

title: 〜やすい / 〜にくい
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Easy to do ~ / Hard to do ~ (ease or difficulty)
Formation: Verb stem + やすい / にくい
Explanation: やすい means 'easy to do'. にくい means 'hard/difficult to do'. Both attach to the verb stem and conjugate like い-adjectives.
Examples: この本は読みやすいです。 - This book is easy to read. | 漢字は書きにくいです。 - Kanji are hard to write. | この道は歩きやすいです。 - This road is easy to walk on.

title: 〜ようです / 〜みたいです
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: It seems that ~ / It looks like ~ (appearance/inference)
Formation: Plain form + ようです / みたいです
Explanation: Both express inference based on observation. ようです is more formal; みたいです is casual. Different from そうです (direct appearance).
Examples: 彼女は疲れているようです。 - She seems to be tired. | 外は寒いみたいです。 - It looks like it's cold outside. | 電車が遅れているようです。 - It seems the train is delayed.

title: 〜かもしれません
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Might ~ / Maybe ~ / Perhaps ~ (possibility)
Formation: Plain form + かもしれません / かもしれない
Explanation: Expresses uncertainty and possibility — lower probability than でしょう. Plain form precedes it; な-adj and nouns drop だ before かもしれません.
Examples: 明日は雨が降るかもしれません。 - It might rain tomorrow. | 彼女は知らないかもしれない。 - She might not know. | これは難しいかもしれませんが、頑張ります。 - This might be difficult, but I'll do my best.

title: 〜ながら
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: While doing ~ (simultaneous actions)
Formation: Verb stem + ながら
Explanation: Indicates two actions happening at the same time by the same subject. The main action comes after ながら.
Examples: 音楽を聴きながら勉強します。 - I study while listening to music. | 歩きながら話しましょう。 - Let's talk while walking. | テレビを見ながらご飯を食べました。 - I ate while watching TV.

title: 〜でも
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Even ~ / Any ~ (inclusive: even this, any at all)
Formation: Noun + でも / Question word + でも
Explanation: でも after a noun means 'even'. After question words (なん、どこ、だれ etc.) it means 'any': なんでも (anything), どこでも (anywhere), だれでも (anyone).
Examples: 子供でも分かる本です。 - It is a book even a child can understand. | なんでも食べます。 - I eat anything. | お茶でもどうですか。 - How about some tea (or something)?

title: 〜ために / 〜のために
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: In order to ~ / For the sake of ~ (purpose or benefit)
Formation: Verb dictionary form + ために / Noun + のために
Explanation: ために expresses purpose (in order to do something) or benefit (for someone's sake). Verb form is always dictionary form.
Examples: 日本語を勉強するために、毎日練習します。 - In order to study Japanese, I practice every day. | 家族のために働いています。 - I am working for my family. | 健康のために運動します。 - I exercise for my health.

title: 〜し〜し
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: And ~ and ~ (listing multiple reasons or qualities)
Formation: Clause 1 + し、Clause 2 + し (〜し)
Explanation: し lists multiple reasons or qualities, implying 'and also'. Softer than から for giving reasons. Often implies 'among other reasons'.
Examples: この街は安全だし、きれいだし、住みやすいです。 - This town is safe, it's clean, and it's easy to live in. | 彼は頭がいいし、優しいし、好きです。 - He's smart, he's kind — I like him. | お腹も空いたし、疲れたし、帰りましょう。 - I'm hungry and tired, so let's go home.

title: 〜たら
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: If ~ / When ~ (conditional: once a condition is met)
Formation: Verb / Adj た-form + ら
Explanation: たら expresses a conditional: once A happens, B follows. More natural than と for hypothetical situations. Also used for 'when' in the past: 着いたら電話した (When I arrived, I called).
Examples: 宿題が終わったら、遊びましょう。 - When you finish your homework, let's play. | 春になったら、お花見をしましょう。 - When spring comes, let's go flower-viewing. | 困ったら、遠慮なく言ってください。 - If you're in trouble, please don't hesitate to say so.

title: 〜ば〜ほど
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: The more ~ the more ~ (proportional increase)
Formation: Verb ば-form / い-adj ければ + Verb/Adj + ほど
Explanation: Expresses that as one thing increases, another increases proportionally. ば-form + same verb/adj + ほど + result.
Examples: 練習すればするほど、上手になります。 - The more you practice, the better you become. | 高ければ高いほど、品質がいいです。 - The more expensive it is, the better the quality. | 知れば知るほど、日本語が面白くなります。 - The more you know, the more interesting Japanese becomes.

title: 〜だけ
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Only ~ / Just ~ (limit or restriction)
Formation: Noun / Verb plain form + だけ
Explanation: だけ limits to only the stated amount or thing. Similar to しか + negative, but だけ has a neutral tone while しか is more emphatic/restrictive.
Examples: 水だけ飲みます。 - I only drink water. | 少しだけ待ってください。 - Please wait just a little. | 一回だけ見せてください。 - Please show me just once.

title: 〜しか〜ない
content:
Romaji: 
Meaning: Nothing but ~ / Only ~ (with emphasis on insufficiency)
Formation: Noun / Amount + しか + Negative verb
Explanation: しか must be followed by a negative verb. Implies the speaker feels the amount is insufficient or surprising. Stronger/more emotional than だけ.
Examples: 百円しかありません。 - I only have 100 yen (and that's not enough). | 日本語しか話せません。 - I can only speak Japanese (nothing else). | 三人しか来ませんでした。 - Only three people came (fewer than expected).

title: Classical Japanese Elements in Modern Japanese
content:
Description: Understand classical Japanese grammar patterns that survive in formal modern Japanese.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: Classical Japanese (文語/古文) appears in proverbs, set phrases, legal texts, formal literature, and signage. N1 candidates must recognize these patterns.
Dialogue: Literary: 為せば成る、為さねば成らぬ何事も。 - If you try, you will succeed; if you do not try, nothing will be achieved. | Proverb: 急がば回れ。 - More haste, less speed. (lit. If in a hurry, take the roundabout way.) | Formal Notice: 関係者以外立入るべからず。 - No entry for unauthorized persons.

title: Nuanced Expressions of Emotion & Psychology
content:
Description: Express subtle emotions and psychological states with precision.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: These expressions appear frequently in formal speeches, literary works, essays, and business correspondence. They convey deep sincerity.
Dialogue: Essay: 彼の無謀な行動に、驚きを禁じ得なかった。 - I could not help but be surprised at his reckless behavior. | Speech: 皆様のご健康とご発展を願ってやみません。 - I sincerely and endlessly hope for your health and development. | Monologue: 知っていながら、言わずにはいられなかった。 - Knowing it, I couldn't help but say it.

title: Logical & Academic Discourse
content:
Description: Master the language of academic papers, debates, and logical argumentation.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: Japanese academic writing heavily uses noun-heavy structures, passive voice, and hedging expressions. Direct assertions are often softened.
Dialogue: Academic: この研究結果をふまえて、新たな仮説を提唱する。 - Based on these research results, I propose a new hypothesis. | Debate: 相手の主張は事実に即していない。 - The opponent's argument is not based on the facts. | Paper: この現象は経済的格差に起因すると見なすことができる。 - This phenomenon can be considered to originate from economic disparities.

title: Four-Character Idioms (四字熟語)
content:
Description: Learn essential four-character compound words derived from Chinese classics.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: 四字熟語 are an important part of Japanese literary and formal culture. Many originate from Chinese classics (漢文) and Buddhist teachings.
Dialogue: A: 彼女の対応は本当に臨機応変で素晴らしい。 - Her ability to adapt to situations is truly wonderful. | B: 試行錯誤を繰り返した末に、ついに解決策が見つかった。 - After repeating trial and error, a solution was finally found. | A: まさに一石二鳥ですね！ - That's exactly killing two birds with one stone!

title: Political, Legal & Economic Vocabulary
content:
Description: Build vocabulary for understanding Japanese news, law, and economic discourse.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: The ability to understand NHK news broadcasts and read newspaper articles is a practical benchmark for N1 level Japanese.
Dialogue: News: 憲法の規定に基づいて、新たな法律が制定された。 - Based on the provisions of the constitution, a new law was enacted. | Analysis: 少子化を背景に、移民政策の見直しが求められている。 - Against the backdrop of a declining birthrate, a review of immigration policy is being called for. | Report: 経済の観点から見ると、この政策は有効だと考えられる。 - From an economic perspective, this policy is considered effective.

title: Formal Written Japanese
content:
Description: Learn the key differences between spoken and written Japanese and formal expression patterns.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: Business Japanese (ビジネス日本語) has its own set of expressions and formulas. Keigo (敬語) — honorific language — is essential in professional settings.
Dialogue: Formal Letter: 拝啓、時下ますますご清栄のこととお慶び申し上げます。 - Dear Sir/Madam, I hope this letter finds you in good health and spirits. | Memo: 本件に関して、ご確認いただきますようお願い申し上げます。 - Regarding this matter, we kindly request your confirmation.

title: Keigo — Honorific Language Deep Dive
content:
Description: Master sonkeigo (respectful), kenjougo (humble), and teineigo (polite) forms.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: Keigo is fundamental to Japanese professional life. Mistakes in keigo can cause significant social friction in formal settings.
Dialogue: Staff: 部長はただいま外出されていらっしゃいます。 - The manager is currently out. | Customer: 田中様はいらっしゃいますか？ - Is Tanaka-sama available? | Staff: 少々お待ちいただけますでしょうか。 - Could you please wait a moment?

title: Complex Sentence Structures
content:
Description: Build complex, multi-clause sentences using advanced connectives.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: 〜以上は and 〜からには both mean "now that / since" but 以上は is slightly more formal.
Dialogue: A: やると決めた以上は、最後まで頑張らなければなりません。 - Now that you have decided to do it, you must persevere until the end. | B: 留学したいとはいえ、お金の問題もあります。 - Although I want to study abroad, there is also the matter of money. | A: 申し込んだものの、まだ詳細が確認できていません。 - Although I applied, I have not yet been able to confirm the details.

title: Reading News & Media Japanese
content:
Description: Learn vocabulary and structures commonly used in Japanese news and media.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: News Japanese often uses passive voice and nominalizations. The style is dense and omits particles more frequently than conversational Japanese.
Dialogue: News: 政府の発表によれば、新たな経済対策が来月から実施される見通しだ。 - According to the government's announcement, new economic measures are expected to be implemented from next month. | News: 物価上昇に伴い、家計への影響が懸念されている。 - Along with the rise in prices, concerns are growing about the impact on household budgets.

title: Expressing Degree & Extent
content:
Description: Express degree, extent, and limits using advanced grammatical patterns.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: 〜だけあって acknowledges that a result is natural given a person's background or effort. It always has a positive or expected nuance.
Dialogue: A: 彼女は努力家だけあって、成績がとても良い。 - As expected of someone who works hard, her grades are very good. | B: 健康でさえあれば、他のことは何でもできる。 - As long as you are healthy, you can do anything else. | A: 彼ほど努力している人はいない。 - There is nobody who works as hard as him.

title: Expressing Reason & Cause (〜ため / 〜せいで / 〜おかげで)
content:
Description: Learn nuanced ways to express reasons and causes, including blame and gratitude.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: おかげで implies positive outcome; せいで implies negative outcome. Using them incorrectly can seem sarcastic.
Dialogue: A: 試験に合格できたのは、先生のおかげです。 - It is thanks to the teacher that I passed the exam. | B: 逆に、私は体調が悪かったせいで、試験に集中できませんでした。 - On the contrary, because of my poor health, I couldn't concentrate on the exam. | A: 来年のためにも、もっと準備をしましょう。 - For next year too, let's prepare more.

title: Expressing Contrast (〜のに / 〜くせに / 〜一方)
content:
Description: Express contrast and unexpected results using various conjunctions.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: くせに is stronger and more critical than のに. It implies the speaker thinks the subject should know better.
Dialogue: A: あんなに勉強したのに、試験に落ちてしまった。 - Even though I studied so much, I ended up failing the exam. | B: 彼は知っているくせに、知らないふりをしている。 - Despite knowing, he is pretending not to know. | A: 都市は便利な一方で、自然が少ない。 - While cities are convenient, on the other hand they lack nature.

title: Potential, Desire & Necessity
content:
Description: Express ability, desires, and necessity using various grammatical forms.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: べきだ expresses a moral obligation or advice; なければならない is a stronger, more external obligation.
Dialogue: A: 彼はいつも新しいゲームを欲しがっています。 - He is always wanting new games. | B: 健康のためには、もっと野菜を食べるべきです。 - For your health, you should eat more vegetables. | A: そうですね。毎日運動する必要がありますね。 - You're right. We need to exercise every day.

title: Quotation & Reported Speech
content:
Description: Learn how to report what others said, thought, or heard.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: Japanese reported speech does not always change tense like English does. Context and time expressions carry tense information.
Dialogue: A: 田中さんによると、新しいカフェが駅の近くにできたそうです。 - According to Tanaka, it seems a new cafe opened near the station. | B: 山田さんは来週旅行に行くと言っていましたよ。 - Yamada said they are going on a trip next week. | A: 部長から、会議が延期されたとのことです。 - I heard from the manager that the meeting has been postponed.

title: Expressing Change & Transformation
content:
Description: Learn how to express gradual or sudden changes in state.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: てくる implies a change coming toward the present from the past; ていく implies a change going away into the future.
Dialogue: A: 日本語を勉強してから、ニュースが聞き取れるようになりました。 - After studying Japanese, I became able to understand the news. | B: 最近、手紙を書く人が少なくなりましたね。 - Recently, the number of people who write letters has decreased. | A: 技術はこれからもっと発展していくでしょう。 - Technology will continue to develop from here on.

title: Giving & Receiving (てあげる / てもらう / てくれる)
content:
Description: Master the complex system of giving and receiving in Japanese.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: The direction of giving/receiving is crucial in Japanese. Using the wrong form can sound unnatural or even rude.
Dialogue: A: 田中さんが荷物を持ってくれました。 - Tanaka carried my bags for me. | B: それは親切ですね。先生に教えていただきましたか？ - That's kind. Did you have the teacher teach you? | A: はい、先生に教えていただきました。とても助かりました。 - Yes, I had the teacher teach me. It was very helpful.

title: Causative & Passive Forms
content:
Description: Learn how to make someone do something, and how to express being acted upon.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: The causative-passive form (させられる) often carries a nuance of being forced to do something against one's will.
Dialogue: A: 部長に残業させられました。 - I was made to work overtime by the manager. | B: それは大変でしたね。私は子供に野菜を食べさせました。 - That must have been tough. I made my child eat vegetables.

title: Expressing Conditions (〜ば / 〜たら / 〜と / 〜なら)
content:
Description: Master the four conditional forms in Japanese and when to use each one.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: と is for natural/automatic consequences. たら is most versatile. ば is often for hypotheticals. なら is for advice based on new information.
Dialogue: A: もし時間があれば、映画を見に行きませんか？ - If you have time, shall we go see a movie? | B: 仕事が終わったら、連絡します。 - When work finishes, I'll contact you. | A: 東京に行くなら、スカイツリーに行ったほうがいいですよ。 - If you're going to Tokyo, you should go to Sky Tree.

title: Expressing Hearsay & Appearance (〜そう / 〜らしい / 〜ようだ)
content:
Description: Learn how to express what things seem like and what you've heard.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: 〜そうだ has two completely different meanings depending on conjugation: verb-stem + そうだ = looks like; plain form + そうだ = hearsay.
Dialogue: A: ニュースによると、明日は雪が降るそうです。 - According to the news, it seems it will snow tomorrow. | B: 本当ですか？空を見ると、確かに曇っているようですね。 - Really? Looking at the sky, it certainly does seem cloudy. | A: 田中さんは風邪を引いたらしいですよ。 - It seems like Tanaka caught a cold.

title: Making Requests & Giving Permission
content:
Description: Learn polite ways to make requests and ask for or give permission.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: Politeness levels matter greatly in Japanese. Using too casual a form with a superior can be seen as disrespectful.
Dialogue: A: すみません、窓を開けてもいいですか？ - Excuse me, is it alright if I open the window? | B: はい、どうぞ。でも、エアコンが入っているので、少しだけにしてください。 - Yes, please go ahead. But since the air conditioning is on, please just a little. | A: わかりました。少し手伝っていただけますか？ - Understood. Could you help me a bit?

title: Greetings & Self-Introduction
content:
Description: Learn essential Japanese greetings and how to introduce yourself.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: In Japan, bowing while greeting is customary. The depth of the bow reflects the level of respect.
Dialogue: A: こんにちは！はじめまして。田中です。 - Hello! Nice to meet you. I am Tanaka. | B: はじめまして。山田です。よろしくお願いします。 - Nice to meet you. I am Yamada. Please treat me well. | A: こちらこそ、よろしくお願いします。 - Likewise, please treat me well.

title: Numbers & Counting
content:
Description: Learn Japanese numbers from 1 to 10,000 and basic counters.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: Japanese has multiple counter systems depending on what is being counted.
Dialogue: A: りんごをいくつ買いますか？ - How many apples will you buy? | B: みっつ買います。 - I will buy three.

title: Family Members
content:
Description: Learn vocabulary for family members in Japanese, including humble and honorific forms.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: Japanese uses different words for your own family (humble) vs. someone else's family (honorific). ちち = my father; おとうさん = your/someone's father.
Dialogue: A: ご家族は何人ですか？ - How many people are in your family? | B: 四人家族です。父と母と妹がいます。 - There are four of us. I have a father, mother, and younger sister. | A: いいですね。私は一人っ子です。 - That's nice. I am an only child.

title: Daily Routine & Time
content:
Description: Learn to talk about daily activities and express time in Japanese.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: Japan uses both the 12-hour and 24-hour clock. Train schedules and official times often use the 24-hour format.
Dialogue: A: 毎朝何時に起きますか？ - What time do you wake up every morning? | B: 六時に起きます。それから、シャワーを浴びて、朝ごはんを食べます。 - I wake up at six. Then I take a shower and eat breakfast. | A: 学校は何時から何時までですか？ - What time is school from and until? | B: 八時半から三時までです。 - It is from 8:30 until 3:00.

title: Food & Ordering at a Restaurant
content:
Description: Learn food vocabulary and how to order food at a Japanese restaurant.
Objectives: 
Key Grammar: undefined
Cultural Note: いただきます is said before eating, expressing gratitude. ごちそうさまでした is said after eating, thanking the cook or host.
Dialogue: Store: いらっしゃいませ。何になさいますか？ - Welcome. What will you have? | A: ラーメンをひとつと、餃子をふたつください。 - One ramen and two gyoza please. | Store: お飲み物はいかがですか？ - What would you like to drink? | A: お茶をください。 - Green tea please.
